clue.text: Invention needing dummy?

parts.note: a person's pet invention is often called their infant, and an infant famously needs a dummy, the rubber teat a British parent gives to soothe it

explanation.walkthrough: A dummy here is the British word for a pacifier; 'invention' points to the idiom of a creation being someone's little one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherished creation is colloquially someone's infant, and real infants need a pacifier.

clue.text: Garment cost? Over a pound

indicators.note: the word for cost covers the other pieces, sitting outside them

parts.note: to be is to cost, as in 'that will be five pounds'
to throb is to pound, as a heart does

explanation.surface: A shopper asks the price of a garment and hears it is more than a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money but is the verb, beat; 'cost' is 'be' as in quoting a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose garment worn before or after bathing.

clue.text: Simpson about to tease gang leader, the bigmouth

indicators.note: the cartoon character goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Bart Simpson of the cartoon
to rag someone is to tease them

indicators.note: the leader of the gang is the one at its front, so take its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cartoon boy teases a gang's boss, being a loudmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart boasts loudly, so is a bigmouth.

clue.text: Is exam result open to appeal so surprising?

definitions.text: Is exam result open to appeal
definitions.meaning: read as ..., a script that can be marked again

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as re-markable: an exam paper open to appeal can be marked a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary or striking is worthy of comment, hence surprising.

clue.text: Always, books kept as record

indicators.note: the books are held inside the word for always

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Books are always kept as a record.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter figures is to record them in a ledger.

clue.text: Discover sectarian at fault

indicators.note: the letters of sectarian are wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Find out that a sectarian figure is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain a fact is to find it out, to discover it.

clue.text: Top man is smooth character, having to reconcile differences

parts.note: K is the king, the top piece in chess or cards
taken as written
to sand is to smooth
a person's make-up is their character

explanation.surface: The boss is a slick operator who has to settle quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a quarrel with affection is an idiom for reconciling differences.

clue.text: Drink makes bishop frisky

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
randy means sexually frisky

explanation.surface: A bishop gets frisky from drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, a drink.

clue.text: Last wind up river

parts.note: to wind up is to end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A final wind blowing up the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or endure over time.

clue.text: In passing opposite points, feature seen outside

indicators.note: the feature is placed around, outside, the pair of compass points

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing feature
N and S, north and south, are opposite points of the compass

explanation.surface: A traveller notes, in passing, a landmark visible between two compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across a place.

clue.text: Sixtus IV's 1 ac first to suffer mutant encephalitis

indicators.note: take the first letter of suffer
mutated letters, changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Pope Sixtus IV's infant is first to catch a mutated brain infection.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' is the answer to 1 across, used in its sense of a cherished creation; Sixtus IV commissioned the chapel named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican's famous chapel was built for Pope Sixtus IV, so it was his pet project.

clue.text: Hot yellow sauce with different starter — now it's for pudding!

indicators.note: the first letter of the sauce is swapped for another one

parts.note: mustard is a hot yellow condiment

explanation.surface: A cook switches from a savoury condiment to a sweet one as the meal moves to dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the M of MUSTARD to C; the clue does not name the new letter, so the definition must confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is the sweet yellow sauce poured over a British pudding, the dessert course.

clue.text: Hospital official getting sense right in the end

indicators.note: sense and right are placed inside the word for the end

parts.note: the rear is the back end
the gist is the general sense

explanation.surface: A hospital doctor finally comes round to good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: A registrar in a British hospital is a senior grade of doctor below consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a doctor of middling seniority, an official grade.

clue.text: Tree (cherry) with leaf oddly backward

indicators.note: the colour and the odd letters, taken together, are read in reverse order

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of leaf

explanation.surface: A cherry tree is described by a peculiar backward-curling leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cherry' in brackets looks like the kind of tree, but it is the colour; 'backward' turns the colour and the leaf's odd letters together as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family, common by rivers.

clue.text: Stop! Police raids ruined local entertainment

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
the Bill is British slang for the police

indicators.note: the letters of raids are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A shout of alarm as a police raid wrecks a night at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is the British word for a nearby pub; bar billiards is a pub table game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar billiards is a table game played in British pubs, a local's entertainment.

clue.text: Bird nicks old underwear for amorous relation

indicators.note: the bird steals, so takes inside it, the other pieces

parts.note: a lory is a type of parrot
a vest is an undershirt in British English

explanation.surface: A bird steals an old vest, which becomes a romantic tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' means a narrative, something related; a vest is British underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance novel or film is a narrative, a relation, about love.

clue.text: No couple rings in to give name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for couple surrounds the word in

parts.note: to mate is to couple
taken as written

explanation.surface: Without a couple's ring, a name is given.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to name them for a post.

clue.text: Keeping bodybuilders in check, so strong

indicators.note: the check holds the bodybuilders inside it

parts.note: to vet is to check
he-men are muscular bodybuilders

explanation.surface: A trainer keeps muscle men under control, so is forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful or strongly felt.

clue.text: O Lord! Where might I seek thee?

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise or dismay
God is traditionally sought in the skies overhead

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a prayer, but the first part is the mild oath and the second the place of the Lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a dated exclamation of surprise and the location of the divine realm.

clue.text: Ignore academic success at university

parts.note: a pass is success in an exam
up means at university in British usage

explanation.surface: Disregard an exam pass at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to ignore or decline it.

clue.text: Uplifting music and dance, perhaps, in song

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up reads the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: music and dance are examples of the arts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Uplifting music and dance are found in song.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or melody, a song.

clue.text: A long letter

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, yearn; the answer is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter H is spelt out in full, as with bee or cee.

clue.text: Poisonous drink?

parts.note: a venomous serpent's attack, which also names a pub mix of lager and cider

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the answer is also a strong drink of lager and cider, notorious for its effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub drink of lager and cider is named after a venomous serpent's attack.

clue.text: A note doctor's prescribed — don't forget it!

parts.note: la is a note in sol-fa
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription note comes with a reminder not to forget it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes the rallying cry 'Remember the Alamo!' of the Texas Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texan battle cry 'Remember the Alamo' urges that the fort never be forgotten.

clue.text: Set partner to find short utensil to hold meat

indicators.note: the shortened utensil surrounds the meat
the utensil loses its last letter

parts.note: a spoon is an eating utensil
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a cutlery partner to go with a small utensil for holding meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set partner' refers to a hairdresser's 'shampoo and set'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser offers a wash followed by a set, so the wash is the set's companion.

clue.text: A pet needing replacement, one pushing up the daisies

indicators.note: the letters of a pet are put back in a different arrangement

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A pet owner mourns an animal that has died and needs replacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead and buried, idiomatically pushing up flowers, is a euphemistic state of rest.

clue.text: Fine chest area spotted?

parts.note: a penalty is a fine
a box is a chest

explanation.surface: A box of fines noticed in some area.
explanation.walkthrough: In football the penalty area contains the penalty spot, so it is 'spotted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The football penalty area holds the penalty spot, making it an area with a spot.

clue.text: Balance somewhat overestimated

indicators.note: only part of the word overestimated is used

explanation.surface: A bank balance has been somewhat overstated.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder or balance of something is what is left over.
